sections.html:
Eddy County fills the southeast corner of New Mexico along the Texas line. Carlsbad is the county seat, Artesia is the other city, and Hope and Loving are villages. The 2020 census counted 62,314 residents: 32,238 in Carlsbad, 12,875 in Artesia, 1,390 in Loving and 15,811 in the rest of the county.

About a quarter of residents live outside any incorporated place, and a rural house is taxed by a different mix of districts than one inside Carlsbad or Artesia. Oil and gas, potash, the federal Waste Isolation Pilot Plant and tourism drive local jobs, so housing demand can swing with drilling and plant schedules. Workers on short assignments often rent, which is why many Eddy County owners end up as landlords.

sections.h2: Who values property and who collects
sections.html:
The Eddy County Assessor values property. The Eddy County Treasurer bills and collects. State law gives the county assessor the valuation job except for railroads, pipelines, utilities, airlines, power plants and mineral property, which the state Taxation and Revenue Department values itself. That carve-out is large in oil country: 531 properties statewide worth $32 billion, about 17 percent of the tax base, sit with the state.

Check the treasurer's page and the assessor's page for current hours before you drive over.

Bills go out by November 1. The first half is due November 10 and the second half April 10 of the following year. You can pay the first half without interest through December 10 and the second half through May 10.

Valuation happens January 1, and the state sets rates around September 1. Treasurers mail bills November 1.

An unpaid tax bill is more than an ordinary debt. State law makes it a lien on real property from January 1 of the tax year, a first lien that ranks ahead of any other interest, recorded or not. No one has to file a notice for the lien to exist, so a search of recorded documents will not reveal it. Ask the treasurer for a current balance before you list or accept an offer.

sections.h2: How valuation works and what changes at sale
sections.html:
While one owner holds a home, its residential value can rise only 3 percent a year. The statute caps it at the higher of 103 percent of the prior year's value or 106.1 percent of the value two years earlier. The cap resets when the property changes hands. It also does not apply in the first year a property is valued, to new improvements, or after a change of use or zoning.

Taxable value is one third of assessed value, and rates are set after yield control adjusts them.

For a seller, the buyer's first-year value is reset to current market value, so the new owner's bill can come in higher than yours. If you have owned for decades, expect buyers to ask about that jump. The $2,000 head of family exemption covers a resident's primary home and drops off after a change of ownership, so the buyer has to claim it again.

  • Transfers to a spouse, or to a child who lives in the home, are among the listed exceptions to "change of ownership."
  • A transfer into a revocable trust for yourself, your spouse or your child is also excepted.
  • A transfer between you and an LLC you own does count as a change of ownership, a New Mexico Court of Appeals decision held.

File a written petition with the county assessor within 30 days of the date the notice of valuation was mailed, or by April 1, whichever is later. An appeal goes to the county valuation protest board, and one seat on that board belongs to a state Taxation and Revenue appraiser.

A timely protest keeps the disputed part of the tax from going delinquent. The other route is to pay first and file a refund claim in district court, due January 10 of the following year.

The state's protest pamphlet lists the statute citations.

Interest starts after the December 10 and May 10 dates. At the end of the third full year of delinquency, the account moves to the state. The Delinquent Property Tax Bureau then reaches out by phone, certified mail, site visits and notices posted on the property. It offers installment agreements and, as a last resort, lists the property for public auction. The law requires an auction in each county every calendar year.

When a property sells at auction, the unpaid tax, penalty, interest and costs come off first, and any remainder goes to the former owner. That is a poor way to leave a house you could have sold.

  • An inherited home may carry bills still mailed to the person who died.
  • Absentee owners of rural parcels may miss notices sent to an old address.

Start with the treasurer's balance, the assessor's record of who owns the land and the minerals, and the county clerk's recorded documents. In New Mexico, a deed or mortgage that is not recorded does not affect title or rights against a later purchaser, so recording matters.

Ask any buyer for the offer in writing, ask who pays recording and title costs, and compare the number against your payoff and any tax due.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, so the schedule mostly depends on how fast the title company can clear the lien and record the deed. Gather the tax balance and a copy of your deed first, and the closing can move faster.

faqs.q: When is Eddy County property tax due?
faqs.a: The first half is due November 10 and the second half April 10. You can pay the first half without interest through December 10, and the second half through May 10.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Eddy County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Eddy County Treasurer at (575) 885-3913 for bills and payments. The office is at 101 W. Greene St., Suite 117, in Carlsbad. Call the Assessor at (575) 885-3813 for valuations and exemptions.

faqs.q: How much can my Eddy County home value increase each year?
faqs.a: A residential value cannot rise more than the higher of 103 percent of last year's value or 106.1 percent of the value two years back. The cap resets when ownership changes.

faqs.q: Is there a New Mexico estate or inheritance tax on an Eddy County house?
faqs.a: No. New Mexico's estate tax was phased out as of January 1, 2005, and the state does not impose an inheritance tax. Federal estate tax can still apply to very large estates.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Eddy County house with property tax owed?
faqs.a: Yes, but the lien runs from January 1 and ranks ahead of other interests, so it has to be paid or settled for the buyer to receive clean title. Get a payoff from the treasurer first.
